description: Domraem DOM-Z-102 classic-ESP32 (LX6, rev v3.x, 4 MB flash) 4-output WS281x controller — the classic bring-up roadmap's desk board and WLED-class deployment exemplar. Data terminals are silkscreened IO18/IO16/IO14/IO2 (top to bottom of the DATA group), verified against a photo of the desk unit; GPIO0=OPT and GPIO1/3=UART are standard-wiring inference, though the UART link itself is hardware-verified through the onboard CH340K bridge (0x1A86:0x7522). The screw terminal at the top of the right rail is silkscreened IO13 and marked "spare" — read directly off the physical board by Yona on 2026-08-02. This CORRECTS an earlier entry that called it IO12 and claimed it drove an onboard relay; that entry rested on a sketch transcription plus a vendor listing note ("Relay configuration (to GPIO12)") that names no terminal and may belong to a different model in the same product family. The board's own capability list mentions no relay. GPIO13 is NOT a strapping pin (classic ESP32 straps are GPIO0/2/5/12/15), so it carries none of the boot risk GPIO12 would have. It is offered here as a claimable output; note it is NOT one of the four fused/level-shifted DATA terminals, so its drive is the raw 3.3 V pad — adequate on the bench, marginal over long runs into 5 V WS281x pixels. GPIO capabilities are listed only for pins the board actually exposes. macOS needs the WCH VCP driver before the CH340K serial port appears at all; see the fw-esp32v3 README.

board_label.label: IO18
board_label.note: data channel 1 (top of the DATA group)

board_label.label: IO2
board_label.note: data channel 4 (bottom); classic-ESP32 strapping pin (boot mode); must be low/floating at reset, which a WS281x data line satisfies — fine as an output once booted

board_label.label: IO13
board_label.note: spare screw terminal at the top of the right rail (silkscreen "IO13" / "spare", read off the physical board 2026-08-02). NOT one of the four fused DATA terminals and not level-shifted: the raw 3.3 V pad drives it. Not a strapping pin (it is MTCK/JTAG, and MTMS/GPIO14 is already a data channel here, so JTAG is not preserved on this board anyway).

gpio.reserved_reason: BOOT strapping pin, wired to the board's BOOT button (silkscreen BOOT/RESET, stacked); not exposed as an output terminal
UART0 TX into the CH340K bridge — the host serial link; driving it drops the link
UART0 RX from the CH340K bridge — the host serial link; driving it drops the link
